cards.back: Systems (CPU, memory, services), applications (errors, latency), infrastructure (flows, interfaces, devices).
Log aggregation, alerting, scanning, archiving, reporting, alert tuning.
Aggregation = collecting and normalizing events; correlation = linking them to reveal a scenario. Aggregation comes first.
Security Information and Event Management: aggregates, normalizes, correlates, alerts, and archives. Platform, not a sensor.
Expected configuration baseline (CIS, STIG) used as a compliance comparator.
Agent = local collection installed on the host; agentless = remote collection without installed software.
Antivirus = malware; DLP = data leaks; vulnerability scanner = measuring the vulnerability surface.
Orchestration = automated chaining of actions (SOAR); packet analyzer = deep traffic inspection.
Transports event messages from devices and systems. Answers "what happened?".
Flow statistics: who talks to whom, port, duration, volume — without packet payloads.
Simple Network Management Protocol: reading device counters and receiving traps.
Security Content Automation Protocol: standardizes compliance/vulnerability measurement to automate benchmarks.
Copies traffic from a port/VLAN to a sensor without interrupting flow; depends on the switch.
Notification triggered by a rule, with severity, context, and recipient: it must be actionable.
A real incident occurred and the alert fired (correct detection).
False positive = alert without a real incident; false negative = real incident without an alert (the most dangerous).
Adjusting thresholds and exclusions in a targeted, documented way, measuring the effect on noise and detection.

cards.front: Why not disable an entire rule?
cards.back: You would also remove detection of real attacks: prefer a precise, justified exclusion.
Dashboard = summary view of alerts and metrics; NMS = consolidation of device status. These are outputs, not sources.
